title: Tarte Tatin
subtitle: Upside-down caramel apple tart in buttery pastry
excerpt: Apples cooked slowly in butter and caramel, topped with pastry and then flipped. One of the great French desserts and worth the nerve of turning it out.
sourceNotes: Created by accident at the Hotel Tatin in Lamotte-Beuvron, France, in the 1880s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best served warm on the day. Pastry can be made and chilled a day ahead.

content.text: This serves 6 and takes about 1 hour 30 minutes including pastry chilling. The critical thing to watch is the caramel: it goes from perfect to burned very fast. Stay at the pan once the sugar starts to colour and take it off the heat the moment it turns a deep amber.
Have a large flat plate ready before you take the tart out of the oven. You flip it while it is still hot so the caramel is liquid enough to run off the apples properly.

items.prepNote: peeled, cored, quartered (about 6 large Cox or Braeburn)

content.text: Make the pastry: rub cold butter into flour and sugar until like breadcrumbs. Mix in yolk and 2 tablespoons cold water until the dough comes together. Flatten into a disc, wrap, and chill 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 200C. In a 24cm ovenproof frying pan or skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add sugar and cook without stirring for 5-7 minutes until deep golden caramel forms.
Remove from heat. Add vanilla. Arrange apple quarters tightly in the caramel, rounded side down. They will shrink as they cook.
Return the pan to a medium heat. Cook the apples for 15 minutes, basting now and then. They are ready when they start to soften and the caramel turns deep amber.
Roll pastry into a circle slightly larger than the pan. Drape over the apples and tuck the edges down inside the pan.
Bake for 25 minutes until pastry is golden and the caramel is bubbling around the edges.
Leave to cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Place a plate larger than the pan over the top. In one confident motion, flip the tart onto the plate. Serve warm with creme fraiche or ice cream.

items.symptom: Caramel is too pale and tastes only of sugar
items.fix: It needs to reach a deep amber, which is darker than you think is safe - keep going

items.symptom: Apples release too much water and the caramel is thin
items.cause: Apples were too ripe or cut too thin
items.fix: Use firm apples and cook uncovered to evaporate the liquid before adding pastry

items.symptom: Apples stuck to the pan when turning out
items.cause: Not rested long enough or caramel set solid
items.fix: Run a knife around the edge, warm the pan base briefly over low heat to re-melt, then turn again

content.text: Tarte tatin is said to have been created by accident at a hotel in the Loire Valley town of Lamotte-Beuvron in the late 1800s. The Tatin sisters accidentally overcooked the apples and placed the pastry on top to salvage the dish. The famous Paris restaurant Maxim's later put it on its menu and made it famous. It is now one of the most recognisable French desserts in the world.
